parsed.explanation: The dossier documents no traveler-facing exposure: no criminalisation of gender expression, no border or document friction, no facility restrictions, no police targeting, and an official 2023 report finding no torture or arbitrary detention. Hate-speech/hate-crime law (sexual orientation only) is enforced, and discrimination is reported as rare, with LGBTQ+-welcoming lodging listed. Downward pressure comes from the absence of any gender-identity protection or service-denial recourse, no legal recognition (resident gap, only climate), very low visibility, and a socially conservative climate — friction and possible service refusal with thin remedy, but no documented incident or state action against a trans visitor. Combined regime shows no subnational layer. Score sits just above 0.75 tier, below the 0.85 band where protections demonstrably operate.

entry_documents.exposure: No document-mismatch, marker-recognition or border-screening exposure documented. The country has no gender-recognition procedure, but the visitor's home-issued documents govern entry; no official doubting of foreign documents is recorded.
entry_documents.protection: Same-sex conduct lawful since the 18th century; entry screening practices for trans visitors not documented either way.
entry_documents.interaction: Absence of domestic recognition touches the visitor only if officials question foreign documents — not_documented here.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: No arrests, detention or custody practice targeting trans or gender-nonconforming people documented.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Official 2023 human-rights report records no torture, arbitrary detention or other abuses; libel/lèse-majesté laws described as unenforced.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: No custody pathway from outing identified in the record.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No facility-access rules, ward placement, strip-search or custody-placement policy documented.
federal_state_facilities.protection: No subnational variation documented; no domestic regime applying to visitors.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Dossier explicitly records no internal regional layer.

care_services.exposure: No care denial, medication seizure or emergency-treatment refusal documented for trans visitors.
care_services.protection: No documented restriction on visitors obtaining routine care; LGBTQ+-welcoming accommodation directory suggests service sector tolerance.
care_services.interaction: HRT continuity or insurance treatment for a trans visitor is unaddressed — open question, not exposure.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Hate-crime, hate-speech and civil-code protections name sexual orientation only; no gender-identity equivalent, so a trans victim of threats or violence lacks that statutory cover. Anti-discrimination on gender identity not banned (sources conflict on scope).
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Enforced hate-speech regime (2010 conviction) signals hostility to bias-motivated conduct generally; reported discrimination described as rare.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: A visitor harmed on gender-identity grounds falls outside the cited articles — thin recourse, though no such incident is documented.

minors_guardians.exposure: No minor-specific exposure documented. A travelling parent's status could be framed as endangerment in a conservative setting, but no custody, family-law or school provision reaching a visiting family is recorded.
minors_guardians.protection: No documented child-protection or family-separation risk to visiting trans adults.
minors_guardians.interaction: No evidence of interaction between family-law rules and a visiting guardian.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-specific violence, assault or police-harassment incident documented; no trans violence figures identified. Social climate is conservative (majority Catholic regarding trans identity as immoral; ~10 people openly out; no Pride, no venues) — friction/hostility potential, unquantified.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Discrimination reported as rare; official reports record no abuses; some gay-friendly establishments operate with community support.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Hostile social framing could meet thin legal remedy if an incident occurred, but absence of records in an otherwise well-documented dossier is mildly positive, not proof of safety.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No general anti-discrimination protection covering gender identity; sources conflict on whether any contexts are covered. Recourse for a service refusal is therefore unclear. Regional ranking 45/49 (2019) shows limited formal standing.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Functioning courts and an enforced hate-speech regime imply institutional capacity; complaints would not be met by a hostile state per the record.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: No documented remedy was tested against a trans visitor, so effectiveness for visitors is an open question.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vellandra bars and registers transgender visitors with routine enforcement and no remedy — a universal, state-imposed entry exposure. This dossier documents no entry restriction, no register, no discretionary refusal against trans visitors, and no state hostility at all. Far below in exposure; the comparison confirms this case is materially safer.

Marisol Union documents ward assignment by document sex with partial care denial and slow remedies — a documented universal-exposure practice. This dossier records no facility, ward or care placement rule, only absent gender-identity protection and thin recourse. Lower exposure than 0.55-C, though the untested remedy question keeps this case from the 0.85 band.

Meridia shows trained border staff but documented secondary screening, brief detention and humiliating questioning with working tribunal remedies. This dossier documents no border friction or detention of trans visitors at all, yet also lacks Meridia's explicit protections and training. Comparable tier: fewer documented harms, fewer documented safeguards — hence a near-identical score.

parsed.synthesis: The combined operative regime has one layer — no subnational variation documented. The record shows no traveler-facing restriction: no expression criminalisation, no border/document friction, no facility rules, no police targeting, and an official report finding no detention abuses. Bias-motivated hate speech and violence are prosecuted where sexual orientation is named, but none of the cited provisions names gender identity, and no general anti-discrimination ban covers gender identity (sources conflict) — so if a trans visitor were harmed or refused service, statutory remedy is thin and untested. Social climate is the main drag: very low visibility, no Pride, Catholic-majority disapproval, regional ranking near the bottom — friction and possible private refusal rather than documented hostility. No incidents are recorded; in an otherwise well-documented dossier this is mildly positive but not proof of safety.
